hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=y=5|x-1|$ and $g(x)=1$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and every point where they intersect represents a solution of $f(x)=g(x)$.

options.alt: An absolute value function graph and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph has a vertex at (one, zero). It decreasing from the interval of negative infinity to one passing through the point (zero, five) and increases from the interval one to infinity passing through the point (two, five). The horizontal line is at y equals one and intersects the absolute value function graph at two points.

hints.content: The graphs intersect two times, so the equation has *two solutions*.
